metadata.name: Commit & Push
metadata.description: Commit and push the current work: check git status, stage only the relevant files (never -A), commit with a clear message, push (rebase onto origin and fix conflicts if the push is rejected). Launch with: /adx-build commit, or /adx-build commit message="your message" to set the commit message explicitly.

parameters.label: Commit message
parameters.description: Optional: the exact commit message to use. If omitted, the agent writes a clear message from the diff.

steps.name: Check status
steps.prompt: Run `git status` and identify exactly which files are modified, added, or deleted. Pick out the files that belong to this session's work (do NOT include unrelated or untracked junk like .DS_Store, logs, editor files). Do not stage or commit anything in this step. Call flow_step_done with a result that lists the files to stage.

steps.name: Stage files
steps.prompt: Stage ONLY the files listed in the previous step, using explicit paths: `git add <file1> <file2> ...`. NEVER use `git add -A` or `git add .` — add your files and your files only. Then verify with `git status` that exactly the intended files are staged (and nothing else). Call flow_step_done when the staging is correct.
steps.nudgePrompt: Re-check `git status`: only the intended files may be staged. Unstage anything extra with `git restore --staged <file>`, then stage the missing files with explicit paths (never `git add -A` / `git add .`). Call flow_step_done once the staging is exact.

steps.name: Commit
steps.prompt: Create the commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`. If the launch parameter `message` was provided, use it verbatim; otherwise inspect the staged diff (`git diff --staged`) and write a clear, conventional message that describes the change (e.g. `feat: ...`, `fix: ...`, `chore: ...`). Verify with `git log -1 --stat` that the commit landed with the right files. Call flow_step_done when done.

steps.name: Push
steps.prompt:
Run `git push`. If the push is rejected because origin has new commits that you don't have:
1. `git fetch origin`
2. Rebase your commit on top of them: `git rebase origin/<branch>` (e.g. `git rebase origin/main`)
3. Fix any conflicts that arise, preserving the intent of both sides, then `git rebase --continue`
4. Run `git push` again.
Prefer rebase over force-push; only use `git push --force-with-lease` if the rebase rewrote commits that were already pushed to the branch. Call flow_step_done only when the push has succeeded (verify with `git status` showing the branch is up to date with origin).
steps.nudgePrompt: The push has not succeeded yet. Check the push error, fetch and rebase onto the latest origin commits, resolve any conflicts, and push again. Call flow_step_done only once `git status` shows the branch is up to date with origin.

steps.name: Summarize
steps.prompt: Produce a one-line summary of what was committed and pushed: commit hash, commit message, branch, and remote state (e.g. `Pushed abc1234 "feat: ..." to origin/main`). Mention if a rebase was needed. Call flow_step_done when done.
